messages.subject: How to do unpaired total copy number analysis
parts:
Hi,

I am wondering whether I can do unpaired total copy number
analysis (49 tumor samples and 137 normal samples) using
aroma.affymetrix package.

Thank you very much!

Alex

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: How to do unpaired total copy number analysis
parts: Hi.

On Tue, Apr 1, 2008 at 6:40 PM, <GZh...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Henrik,
>
> Are you referring me to look at 'Calculating raw total copy numbers
> manually' in the vignettes?

I was mainly thinking of the 'Total copy number analysis (10K, 100K,
500K)' vignette which is for the 500K platform you are using.

> I am wondering whether there is a way to specify two groups of test
> and reference samples
> respectively before normalization.

I see. No, there is no automatic feature in aroma.affymetrix that
allows you to tag samples "normal" and "non-normal" so that all
downstream methods are aware of this difference and deals with it
specifically.

There are basically two ways to deal with the problem of heterogeneity
of samples:

1) Assume that the majority of your samples are normal (diploid) at
any random locus and rely on the robustness of the estimators not to
be biased by outliers (CN aberrations).
2) Estimate the normalization functions "manually" on the normal
samples only and then apply the fitted function to all samples.

Please see thread 'quantile normalization target distribution' on
March 1, 2008 [ http://tinyurl.com/2rag8x ] on how to do this. You
basically have to setup an AffymetrixCelSet that contains only your
normal samples and then estimate the target distribution from this
one. You can then specify to use that distribution when you setup
your QuantileNormalization method. [I'll see if I can simplify this
process slightly in a future release, but for now, please see the
about thread].

Cheers

/Henrik

Thanks Henrik. I am looking over the 'Total copy number analysis (10K,
100K, 500K)'
and wondering what are the paths for two folders named
'annotationData' and 'rawData'
shown in the example. Are they under the same directory?

I basically wanted to try the code below:

name <- "AGRF_2007a"
chipTypes <- c("Mapping250K_Sty")
cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile
$fromChipType(chipType)})

But I ended up getting:

> cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)})
Error in list("lapply(chipTypes, FUN = function(chipType) {" =
<environment>, :

object. No CDF file with that chip type found: Mapping250K_Sty

at throw.default("Could not create ", class(static)[1], " object. No
CDF file

file with tha

I put the three annotation files in the folder:

annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty/

and a test .cel file in the folder:

annotationData/rawData/AGRF_2007a/Mapping250K_Sty/

Thanks much,

Alex

Thanks Henrik. I also figured that out and it is all good now.
I tried to test the code in the page for 'Total copy number analysis
(10K, 100K, 500K)'
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis

So far so good but except for the code:

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)

The error message was:

> rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)
Error in list("calculateResiduals(plm, verbose = verbose)" =
<environment>, :

[2008-04-02 01:29:34] Exception: calculateResiduals() does not yet
support chip effects for which allele A and allele B have been
combined.
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("calculateResiduals() does not yet support chip
effects for w
at throw("calculateResiduals() does not yet support chip effects for
which all
at calculateResidualSet.ProbeLevelModel(this, ...)
at calculateResidualSet(this, ...)
at calculateResiduals.ProbeLevelModel(plm, verbose = verbose)
at calculateResiduals(plm, verbose = verbose)

Any suggestions to correct this?

Thanks,
Alex


The code I used is:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "AGRF_2007a"
chipTypes <- c("Mapping250K_Sty")
cdfs <- lapply(chipTypes, FUN=function(chipType) {AffymetrixCdfFile
$fromChipType(chipType)})

print(cdfs)
gis <- lapply(cdfs, getGenomeInformation)
print(gis)
sis <- lapply(cdfs, getSnpInformation)
print(sis)

cesNList <- list()
chipType <- chipTypes[1]
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
cs <- extract(cs, !isDuplicated(cs))
print(cs)

qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs)
print(qn)

csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)

plm <- RmaCnPlm(csN, combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE)
print(plm)

fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm, verbose=verbose)

Please read the reference listed in the vignette(s), i.e.:

H. Bengtsson; R. Irizarry; B. Carvalho; T.P. Speed, Estimation and
assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics 2008. [pmid: 18204055] [doi:
10.1093/bioinformatics/btn016]

It explains what we mean by "raw CNs" and how they are calculated.

I have added a subsection to both CN vignettes with a code example how
to extract the actually raw CNs.

>
> Moreover, in the above page, at the end, you mentioned "Identification
> of copy-number regions (CNRs)"
> and "GLAD". What does exactly mean by 'copy-number regions'? Are you
> referring to "copy-number
> abnormal regions"?

Yes. Please see the help for the GLAD package and the publication for
its model for more details.

>
> Also on the page of 'Calculating raw total copy numbers manually', it
> says that

> 'cesN' '.
> My question is how to get 'cesN'. Does it have anything to do with
> 'csN' in the page of
> 'Total copy number analysis (10K, 100K, 500K)'.

I use the 'ces' for reffering to a (Cn)ChipEffectSet and 'cs' for an
(Affymetrix)CelSet. 'cesN' is indicating a normalized
CnChipEffectSet. See Vignette 'Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 &
6.0)' for an example. In the Vignette 'Total copy number analysis
(10K, 100K, 500K)' there are two chip types merged so there everything
is put into a 'cesNList' list object. So, to follow the 'Calculating
raw total copy numbers manually' vignette you obviously have to work
with cesN <- cesNList[["Mapping250K_Nsp"]] and then cesN <-
cesNList[["Mapping250K_Sty"]].
